title: the birth of the cousins
hook: the cousins grow up under one roof, and a rivalry is born with them

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kunti's mantra called Dharma, Vayu and Indra, and three sons were born. Justice, strength, and skill.

A fruit tree in a royal garden, boys up in its branches reaching for fruit. Below stands Bhima, the second son of Pandu. He kicks the trunk, and the boys come tumbling down with the fruit. In the water he holds his cousins under until they gasp. In the dust he drags them by the hair. The Mahabharata says he meant no malice; it was a boy's play. But one of the boys on the ground is Duryodhana, the eldest son of Dhritarashtra. And he doesn't forget.
screen: `A TREE FULL OF COUSINS.` → `BHIMA KICKS THE TRUNK.` → `DURYODHANA DOESN'T FORGET.`

segments.voice: The story moves quickly now. Madri, with Kunti's help, has twin sons, Nakula and Sahadeva. In Hastinapura, Gandhari's sons are born, Duryodhana the eldest. In the forest, Pandu dies. Sages bring Kunti and the five sons of Pandu to Hastinapura, and the two families of cousins live in one palace, studying, eating and playing together. Bhima is stronger than all of them, and never lets them forget it. Duryodhana watches, and the story says jealousy takes hold of him. So he arranges a day of water sports by the Ganga, with pavilions and food. Into Bhima's food goes poison. When Bhima, worn out and heavy, lies down by the river, Duryodhana binds him and pushes him into the water. Bhima sinks down into the realm of the Nagas, the serpent people. The snakes bite him, and in the story their venom works against the poison. The Naga king receives him, and Bhima is given a drink that makes him stronger still. Back in Hastinapura, the brothers come home without him. Kunti is frantic and says aloud what she suspects. Vidura tells her to keep quiet: if she accuses Duryodhana openly, he may turn on her other sons. Then Bhima walks home, alive and stronger, and tells his brothers everything. Yudhishthira's answer: say nothing for now, and guard one another. The cousins were born in one family. Now something else has been born between them.
screen: `TWO FAMILIES, ONE PALACE.` · `POISON AT THE RIVER.` · `RESCUED AMONG THE NAGAS.` · `KEEP QUIET, AND KEEP WATCH.` · then, large: `A GRUDGE IS BORN TOO.`

segments.voice: Let a face come back from childhood, someone you grew up beside, and one small moment between you: a game, a fight, a shared meal. If an old sting is still there, notice where it sits; if there's warmth, let it stay a while.
Naga, the serpent people below the waters, whose venom worked against the poison in Bhima's blood and left him stronger still.
Your line: a grudge that started young. Tomorrow, a secret older than all the cousins. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Hindu families tell the Mahabharata to children a piece at a time, and the boyhood of Bhima and Duryodhana, with the poisoned meal and the serpent realm, is one of the pieces told.

original.note: Sanskrit nāga: a serpent; in the story, the serpent people whose realm lies below the waters.

chat.says: How did Bhima survive being poisoned and thrown into the river?
options: The Nagas' venom fought the poison, and he came home even stronger.
Vidura found him on the riverbank and gave him a cure in secret.
Kunti called on the god of the wind, and Vayu lifted him out.
chat.meaning: Duryodhana poisoned Bhima and threw him in the river. Among the Nagas, the snakes' venom worked against the poison, and he came back stronger.

Naga.meaning: the serpent people, living below the waters

notes: All paraphrase. Days 722–726 were not on disk when this was written; this day takes the cousins' boyhood (Bhima's play, the poisoning, the Naga realm) as the close of the arc. If an earlier day already told the poisoning, this day needs a new angle.
Confirm in Ganguli: Bhima's rough play (shaking boys from trees, ducking them in water, dragging them) and the text's statement that it was without malice.

Confirm: Duryodhana binds the sleeping Bhima and throws him into the Ganga; the snakes' venom counters the poison; the Naga king (Vasuki, with Aryaka) gives him a strength-giving drink. Numbers in the source (bowls drunk, days slept, strength of elephants) are deliberately left out.
Confirm Vidura's counsel to Kunti to keep silent, and Yudhishthira's advice to his brothers to say nothing and guard one another.
